findings.message: `ticket_menu_inputs` runs `await ticket_pending(ctx.git, ctx.root, stem)` once for every stem in `set(tickets) | set(invalid) | set(last)`. That set includes every merged or settled stem in the journal, and `ticket_pending` (chupa/runner.py:544) starts a separate `git status --untracked-files=all -- tickets/<stem>/` subprocess. Before this diff, `snapshot` made one porcelain call through `uncommitted_tickets`. This repo has 527 ticket files, so each extension refresh now starts hundreds of git processes, and for unsettled admitted stems it also runs a `git show main:` per stem.
findings.paved_road: Read porcelain once with `--untracked-files=all` (or reuse the entries `plan_intake` already reads), then derive each stem's `pending` flag from that single listing using the same `tickets/<stem>/` prefix test. Keep the flag's meaning the same as `runner.ticket_pending`.

findings.message: `run_ticket = validated(...)` runs `validate_ticket` on the disk text of every stem with a file, including every merged or settled ticket that `load_tickets` deliberately skipped ('Full engine parse of unsettled tickets only'). `order_ticket` and `review_ticket` can add up to two more calls per stem. `validate_ticket` calls `_graph(repo)` (chupa/tickets.py:544), which reads every `tickets/*/ticket.md`. Each snapshot therefore does O(N²) ticket file reads, about 280k or more for this repo's 527 tickets, where it used to do O(N).
findings.paved_road: Build the ticket graph once per snapshot and pass it into validation, for example with an edges parameter on `validate_ticket` that the verbs also use, or a per-call cache inside `tickets.py`. Either way the admission inputs stay the same values the verbs compute, without rescanning the whole tickets tree for every stem.
